headline: Nifty rose an eighth day while *more stocks fell*
subline: FIIs bought Rs 7,212.22 Cr. DIIs sold almost the same.
hero_text: India VIX stayed at 17.42, near its 21 session high, even as the Nifty notched an eighth straight gain.

why.title: An eighth straight gain
why.desc: Nifty added 58.25 pts to close at 25,044.65.

why.title: FIIs bought, DIIs sold evenly
why.desc: FIIs net bought Rs 7,212.22 Cr while DIIs net sold Rs 7,172.53 Cr.

why.title: Pharma and PSU banks led
why.desc: PSU Banks rose 3.73% and Pharma gained 1.65%.

sector_reasons.PSU Bank: SBI led a broad PSU lender bid
sector_reasons.Pharma: Divi's Lab and Laurus hit 52 week highs
sector_reasons.Bank: SBI and private lenders lifted the index
sector_reasons.Metal: Tata Steel slid as metals gave way

bonus_text: FIIs net bought Rs 7,212.22 Cr and DIIs net sold Rs 7,172.53 Cr. Near mirror images, and the Nifty still edged up.
movers_note_gainers: SBI led at 2.56%. Trent, Nestle, NTPC and L&T each added over 1.8%.
movers_note_losers: Tata Steel fell most at 2.81%. HCLTech, UltraTech, ITC and Bajaj Finance trailed.
watch_text: 25,000 held the heaviest put OI and max pain. 26,000 held the heaviest call OI. Wednesday reopens after a holiday.
lessons: The streak ran on a thin base. 28 of the Nifty 50 fell and the wider market skewed red.
Fear stayed high through the rally. VIX sat near the top of its 21 session range.
Flows netted out. Foreign buying and domestic selling matched almost exactly.
The tail lagged the head. Smallcap 250 slipped while the Nifty rose.
alert_text: Wednesday 11 November reopens after the Tuesday holiday. HUL and ONGC go ex dividend on Thursday.
cta_headline: Eight up days, thin base. *Wednesday reopens the test*.
cta_sub: Markets shut Tuesday. The next bell is Wednesday 11 November.
next_text: Wednesday 11 November reopens after the Tuesday holiday. HUL and ONGC go ex dividend a day later.
caption_a:
Eight straight gains, yet more stocks fell than rose.
Nifty closed at 25,044.65, up 0.23%. Breadth ran 1,126 up to 1,583 down.
FIIs bought Rs 7,212.22 Cr. DIIs sold Rs 7,172.53 Cr.
Watch: 25,000 held the heaviest put OI. Markets shut Tuesday, next bell Wednesday.
